title: Lapatinib-Based Radioagents for Application in Nuclear Medicine
content: Lapatinib is an approved therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer. It has a high affinity for the non-receptor cytoplasmic tyrosine kinases of the EGFR and HER2 receptors. It is a reversible type II inhibitor, with Kiapp values ​​of 3 nM and 13 nM, respectively. The dissociation rate of the lapatinib–receptor complex is notably slow compared with many other kinase inhibitors.. Although the literature contains numerous reports on radiolabelled ligands for HER-family receptors, studies on radiolabelled tyrosine kinase inhibitors are far fewer and only few focus specifically on radiolabelled lapatinib. The aim of this review is to compile and discuss the chemical and biological data on lapatinib-based radiopharmaceuticals with potential applications in the diagnosis and treatment of HER2-positive tumors.
